statement: High sensor noise combined with high gripper delay and small object size causes missed grasps due to perception-error-induced misalignment.
mechanism: Sensor noise corrupts perceived cube position; gripper delay means the grasp command uses stale perception; small size leaves no margin for error, so fingers close at the wrong location and miss the cube entirely.
prediction: Increasing retry_count to at least 1 should allow fresh perception on retry and eliminate MISSED_GRASP failures in this region.

statement: Low friction combined with high mass causes slip on lift due to insufficient grip force.
mechanism: High mass increases inertial load during lift; low friction reduces maximum tangential force before slip; current grip_force (15 N) may be too low to hold the cube.
prediction: Increasing grip_force should reduce SLIPPED_ON_LIFT failures in this region.

statement: High sensor noise combined with low friction and low gripper delay causes missed grasps due to perception error and insufficient grip force to compensate.
mechanism: Sensor noise causes position error; low friction means even small misalignment leads to slip; low delay means grasp closes quickly but at wrong position, resulting in missed grasp.
prediction: Increasing both grip_force and retry_count should reduce MISSED_GRASP failures in this region.

statement: Small object size combined with high gripper delay causes missed grasps due to delayed closure on a small target.
mechanism: Small objects require precise finger placement; high delay means the cube may move or perception is outdated by the time the grasp command executes, leading to missed grasps.
prediction: Adding retry_count should allow re-perception and successful grasp, reducing MISSED_GRASP failures in this region.
